title: all is closed under septuple — a machine-checked theorem of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit
description:
all is closed under septuple — decided over the whole of its finite domain by exhaustion, every case walked by the Lean 4 kernel. Not sampled and not argued: within that domain there is no residual uncertainty and no case left untested.

Statement (Lean):

[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8].all (fun d => [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8].contains (m9 (7 * d)))

Statement (LaTeX):

\forall d \in [0,\,1,\,2,\,3,\,4,\,5,\,6,\,7,\,8],\; \mathrm{m9}\mathopen{}\left(7 \cdot d\right) \in [0,\,1,\,2,\,3,\,4,\,5,\,6,\,7,\,8]

What this record establishes. A dated, public, citable deposit of this declaration and its machine-checked proof, recomputable from the source it names — sorry-free, axiom-free, and free of any Mathlib dependency. That is priority, and the record proves it on its own. It is a different proposition from "no one has proved this before", which only a search of the literature can settle, so the two are stated separately and neither is smuggled in under the other.

Novelty: UNCLASSIFIED — an open question, not a claim. No prior-art search has been performed for this source file, so this record asserts priority of deposit and nothing about the literature.

Scope, stated as plainly as the claim. The declaration is decided over a finite domain. It settles no Clay Millennium Problem, asserts no quantum speedup, and describes no physical system. 0/7.
